title: Investigate and remediate kernel-selection regression causing throughput drop on mixed-length workloads
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Summary: After 1.20.1 scheduler changes and a passive attention-optimization flag flip in canary, we observed ~25-40% throughput regressions for production mixed-sequence traffic (short + long sequences). The regression surfaced through elevated queueing and increased token latency on dedicated pools serving 8xA100 nodes. This ticket captures the RCA, mitigations already applied, and tracked action items to prevent recurrence.
timeline: 2026-02-18 02:12 UTC: Pager alert - sustained tail latency increase on dedicated-prod-us-east-1 pool (alert: inference.latency.p50 > 200ms)
2026-02-18 02:20 UTC: On-call (Marco) triage - noticed token throughput drop and scheduler backpressure metrics rising
2026-02-18 03:00 UTC: Canary rollback of attention-optimization flag (deployed to two hosts) - initial micro-improvement only

2026-02-18 04:10 UTC: Identified abnormal kernel selection pattern for multi-length batches; scheduler started favoring a single large-sequence kernel path even when majority of batch items were short
2026-02-18 06:45 UTC: Emergency mitigation - pin scheduler kernel heuristic to pre-1.20 behavior for affected pools (hotfix runtime-1.20.2-hotfix1)
2026-02-19 10:30 UTC: Deploy hotfix across all dedicated pools; metrics returned to expected baseline over next 90 minutes
2026-02-20 09:00 UTC: Post-incident meeting with runtime, scheduler, and inference teams to assign RCA owners and action items
root_cause: A change to the scheduler's sequence-length aggregation heuristic (merged in runtime-1.20.1) combined with a new attention-optimization codepath caused the kernel selector to bias toward a single 'long-seq optimized' kernel. For mixed batches, that kernel path had worse amortized memory traffic and poorer vectorization for short sequences, producing worse throughput. The regression was amplified by continuous batching heuristics that allowed heterogeneous sequences in the same batch without re-evaluating kernel selection after padding adjustments.
mitigations_taken: Pinned scheduler heuristic to previous behavior (hotfix runtime-1.20.2-hotfix1) to restore stable kernel selection
Rolled back attention-optimization flag in canary and staged fleet until further validation
Throttled autoscaling bursts for affected pools to reduce inter-host variance while hotfix propagated
Added temporary alert that monitors kernel-selection distribution per-pool to detect skew

ENG-12543-A7: Run audit of continuous batching heuristics to ensure kernel choice is stable after padding and KV cache lookups (owner: Marco Chen, due: 2026-03-18)
ENG-12543-A8: Update runbook with explicit rollback and hotfix steps for kernel-selection regressions (owner: SRE - Elena Ruiz, due: 2026-03-10)
